title: Add Strassen-Winograd layer for GF(2) BitMatrix multiply
description:
Add a Strassen-Winograd layer above the existing GF(2) M4RM matrix multiplication path, with benchmark-driven crossover selection.

## Background

`64c88ae4` and `dev/bench_results/2026-04-26-uncompetitiveness-profile.md` show GF(2) matrix multiplication at n=1024..4096 is only about 0.13-0.21x of M4RI. M4RI switches to Strassen-Winograd at large sizes; gf2-core currently uses pure schoolbook/M4RM. SIMD routing helps but cannot close the algorithmic exponent gap by itself.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] A Strassen-Winograd multiplication path exists for square GF(2) `BitMatrix` multiplication above an empirically selected crossover, while existing M4RM/scalar fallbacks remain available below the crossover.
- [hard] Correctness is covered by deterministic edge tests and property tests against the existing `BitMatrix::mul` semantics, including n in {0, 1, 63, 64, 65, 127, 128, 129, 256, 512} and at least one larger release-only benchmark validation size.
- [hard] The implementation preserves tail masking and introduces no `unsafe` outside `gf2-kernels-simd`.
- [hard] Benchmark evidence records the selected crossover and compares pre/post throughput against the pinned gf2 baseline and the `64c88ae4` M4RI ratios where available.
- [hard] `cargo-ci` and `code-review` gates pass.
- [aspirational] GF(2) matmul at n>=1024 closes at least half of the residual gap to M4RI after the Tier-A/B kernel work lands.
